TEXT.dm:
Here's what she sent, and what he replied 🤍

Her (11:42 PM): "I was looking forward to tonight. I'm not going to wait by the phone. Take care."
Him (12:03 AM): "You're right. I messed up. Tomorrow, 8 PM. I'll be at your door at 7:55."

He knocked at 7:50. With flowers. She never had to chase him again.

Why it works: She didn't beg, accuse or ask why. She said how she felt and stopped waiting, on her terms. Calm boundaries get respect; long paragraphs get left on read.

The words come from "What Do I Text Back?". All 3 dateunoa ebooks are in my bio if you want the rest.

REPLY.dm:
Here's what she sent, and what he answered 🤍

Her (1:09 AM): "I'm glad you're okay. I'm not going back to what we were."
Him (1:12 AM): "I know. I didn't text to get you back. I texted to say sorry for how I left. You deserved a goodbye."

She wrote back: "Thank you. I hope you find peace too." Then she slept better than she had in four months.

Why it works: One calm sentence closed the door without a fight. No history lesson, nothing for him to argue with. And it left room for the apology she was owed.

ASK.dm:
Here are the exact words he used, and her answer 🤍

Him, at the counter: "Sofia, would you like to have dinner with me on Friday? Just the two of us."
Her, that night: "Yes. Friday at 7. And I have to tell you something about every Saturday :)"

At dinner she told him: every Saturday, she made his coffee a little slower, hoping he'd finally ask.

Why it works: It's clear (dinner, Friday, a date, not 'we should hang out sometime'), it's kind, and it's easy to answer either way. Clarity is what makes a woman feel safe saying yes.
